{{Current events|year=2020|month=04|day=16|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Health and environment
*[[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**The number of confirmed [[Coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]] cases passes two million worldwide. [https://foreignpolicy.com/2020/04/16/coronavirus-cases-double-two-weeks-pass-two-million-worldwide/ (Foreign Policy)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Africa]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Eswatini]]
****[[Eswatini]] reports the country's first death from COVID-19, as total cases rise to 17. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/health-pmn/eswatini-records-first-coronavirus-death-health-minister (National Post)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Nigeria]]
**** At least 18 people in Nigeria have been killed by police during the enforcement of measures to curb the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.telegraaf.nl/nieuws/352972282/corona-bloedbad-in-nigeria-politie-schiet-18-mensen-dood (de Telegraaf)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Europe]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[government of the United Kingdom|government]] extends the country's lockdown for at least another three weeks. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52313715 (BBC)]
****The [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] critical care [[NHS Nightingale Hospital Birmingham]] is opened inside the [[National Exhibition Centre]] in [[Solihull]], [[England]]. It can treat up to 4,000 COVID-19 patients. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-52309494 (BBC)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Germany]]
****The [[Robert Koch Institute]] reports 2,866 new confirmed cases and 315 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest daily death toll in the country to date, bringing [[Germany]]'s death toll to 3,569 and 130,450 total cases. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-germany-cases/germanys-coronavirus-cases-rise-by-2866-deaths-by-315-rki-idUKKCN21Y0KB (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*Police discover the bodies of 17 people inside a [[morgue]] built for four at a nursing home in [[New Jersey]], United States, following an anonymous tip-off. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-52314860 (BBC)]
*[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in India]]
**[[Tablighi Jamaat]] leader [[Muhammad Saad Kandhlawi]] is charged with [[manslaughter]] after a gathering the organization held in [[Delhi]] on March 3 was linked to 1,023 coronavirus cases across 17 [[India]]n states. Police say he ignored two notices to end the religious event at a [[mosque]] in Delhi, though he denies any wrongdoing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-52306879 (BBC)]
*[[Saudi Arabia]] [[capital punishment in Saudi Arabia|executes]] a 33-year-old [[Yemenis|Yemeni]] man convicted for an attack on a Spanish [[dance troupe]] last year, which resulted in two dancers injured. The attack was claimed by the affiliate of [[al-Qaeda]] in the region. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/04/saudi-arabia-executes-yemeni-man-attacked-spanish-performers-200416115627559.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Brazil]], [[Impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic on politics]]
**[[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] fires Health Minister [[Luiz Henrique Mandetta]] amid disagreements over the federal government's response to the coronavirus pandemic. He is replaced by [[Nelson Teich]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/04/16/americas/brazil-health-minister-fired-intl/index.html (CNN)]
